patch_description: The current algorithm sends every partition of every destination along the same single Dijkstra shortest path, causing all traffic to concentrate on one route. This new approach computes k-shortest simple paths (k=4) per destination using nx.shortest_simple_paths with edge cost as weight, then distributes partitions across these candidate paths using a load-aware assignment: partitions are assigned round-robin to candidate paths ordered by cost, with per-edge congestion tracking (edge_load counter) and a congestion penalty (edge cost + congestion_weight * load) to avoid overloading cheap links. This reduces total cost by exploiting alternate low-cost parallel routes and balancing load across multi-network topologies. Key parameters: K_PATHS=4 candidate paths per destination, CONGESTION_WEIGHT=0.5 penalty per concurrent use of an edge, and round-robin partition assignment instead of duplicating a single path.
